extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for petitions to revive abandoned or lapsed patent applications (including terminal disclaimers and provisional application limits), and the rules for arranging, conducting, and recording interviews with examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of unintentional delay for 37 CFR 1.137(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(b) must be accompanied by a statement that the entire delay in providing the required reply from the due date for the reply until the filing of a grantable petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(b) was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Office will generally require only the statement that the entire delay was unintentional, the Commissioner may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional. Where there is such question, the Office may require an applicant to carry the burden of proof to establish that the delay was unintentional within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7) and 37 CFR 1.137(b). See Application of G, 11 USPQ2d at 1380.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement under 37 CFR 1.137(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under either 37 CFR 1.137(a) or 1.137(b) must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer (and fee), regardless of the period of abandonment, in: (A) a design application; (B) a nonprovisional utility application filed before June 8, 1995; or (C) a nonprovisional plant application filed before June 8, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terminal disclaimer must dedicate to the public a terminal part of the term of any patent granted thereon equivalent to the period of abandonment, and must also apply to any patent granted on any continuing application entitled under 35 U.S.C. 120 to the benefit of the filing date of the application for which revival is sought. The requirement does not apply to lapsed patents. Filing a terminal disclaimer is not a substitute for showing unavoidable or unintentional delay; it cannot excuse an intentional delay nor will unavoidable/unintentional delay waive the disclaimer requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.183 to waive terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant considers the requirement for a terminal disclaimer inappropriate, applicant should file a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 (with fee) to request a waiver of the terminal disclaimer requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of such a petition is strictly limited to extraordinary situations where 'justice requires' relief. Examples include: (A) abandonment caused no actual delay in prosecution (e.g., revived solely for copendency with a continuing application whose prosecution was unaffected, or awaiting Board decision during abandonment); or (B) the patent term is otherwise capped by the 20-year patent term under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) (e.g., revival sought solely for copendency with an application filed on or after June 8, 1995, or where the 20-year term would be longer than 17 years from grant less the period of abandonment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Forms PTO/SB/62 and PTO/SB/63 for terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms PTO/SB/62 and PTO/SB/63 may be used when filing a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.137(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/62 is 'Terminal Disclaimer to Accompany Petition (Period Specified)'; PTO/SB/63 is 'Terminal Disclaimer to Accompany Petition (Period of Disclaimer to be Completed by Petitions Examiner)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and showing for requests for reconsideration under 37 CFR 1.137(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application or lapsed patent must be filed within 2 months of the decision refusing to revive or within such time as set in the decision. This time period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 unless the decision indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.137(d) specifies when a renewed petition will be considered timely. If a renewed petition, request for reconsideration, or other petition seeking review of a prior 1.137 decision is filed outside the specified time period, the Office may require a specific showing as to how the entire delay was 'unavoidable' (1.137(a)) or 'unintentional' (1.137(b)). A delay resulting from deliberately choosing not to persist in seeking revival cannot be considered unavoidable or unintentional; subsequent events or discovery are immaterial to such intentional delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of 37 CFR 1.137 to provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 applies to a provisional application abandoned for failure to reply to an Office requirement. A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) must be accompanied by any outstanding reply to an Office requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5) regards a provisional application as abandoned 12 months after its filing date and not subject to revival thereafter. 37 CFR 1.137(e) allows a provisional application to be revived so as to be pending for no longer than twelve months from its filing date; under no circumstances will a provisional application be pending after twelve months from its filing date. A petition may be filed later than 12 months only to revive the application for the 12-month period following filing, but the application will not be pending after the 12-month limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's written statement under 37 CFR 1.181
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.181 provides that the examiner 'may be directed by the Commissioner to furnish a written statement within a specific time setting forth the reasons for his or her decision upon the matters averred in the petition, supplying a copy thereof to the petitioner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless requested, however, such a statement should not be prepared. See MPEP § 1002.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and destruction of abandoned applications (37 CFR 1.14(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete applications (§ 1.51(a)) which are abandoned may be destroyed and hence may not be available for access or copies after 20 years from their filing date, except those to which particular attention has been called and which have been marked for preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As explained in MPEP § 1302.07, a retention label is used to indicate applications not to be destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulling and forwarding abandoned application files
rubrics_metrics.description: Files of abandoned applications are pulled and forwarded to the Files Repository on a biweekly basis 1 month after the full 6-month statutory period has expired; however, the date of abandonment is after midnight of the date on which the shortened statutory period, including any extensions under 37 CFR 1.136, expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should be carefully scrutinized by the appropriate examiner to verify they are actually abandoned. Check files containing a decision of the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences for presence of allowed claims to avoid erroneous forwarding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering patented and abandoned files (PALM procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patented and abandoned files are ordered by means of a PALM video display transaction by inputting examiner PALM location code, employee number, and patent/application numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After transmission, the PALM response informs whether the request is: (A) accepted; (B) accepted but stored off site (increased delivery time); (C) not accepted since file not located at repository/warehouse; (D) not accepted since a previous request has not yet been filled; or (E) not accepted since the patent/application number input is not valid. Drawings (if any) are normally stored within the file wrapper and delivered with the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying applicants of abandonment (PTOL-1432)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Examining Corps currently mails to the correspondence address of record a Notice of Abandonment form PTOL-1432 in all applications which become abandoned in the Corps for failure to prosecute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere failure to receive a notice of abandonment does not affect the status of an abandoned application. Applicants must act promptly after receiving notice; failure to do so may foreclose relief. If lack of diligent action is predicated on nonreceipt, it may indicate a problem with the correspondence address — a paper notifying the Office of a change of address should be filed promptly (see MPEP §§ 402 and 601.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of abandonment received after allowance or issue fee paid
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of a letter of abandonment while an application is allowed is acknowledged by the Publishing Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An express abandonment arriving after the issue fee has been paid will not be accepted without a showing of one of the reasons indicated in 37 CFR 1.313(b), or else a showing under 37 CFR 1.183 justifying suspension of 37 CFR 1.313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and citation of abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications (when published) are printed publications and are cited as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(b) effective from the date of publication in the Official Gazette. An application or portion thereof from which such was prepared may be used as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) effective from the actual date of filing in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These publications may be used alone or in combination with other prior art in rejecting claims under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103. Defensive Publications and Abstracts have particular historical numbering and listing practices in examiner search files and Official Gazette citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and general policy on interviews (37 CFR 1.133)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview is the personal appearance of an applicant, attorney, or agent before the examiner or a telephone conversation or video conference or electronic mail between such parties presenting matters for the examiner's consideration. Interviews with examiners concerning applications and other matters pending before the Office must be had in the examiners’ rooms at such times, within office hours, as the respective examiners may designate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should be arranged in advance. Interviews for the discussion of the patentability of pending applications will not be had before the first official action thereon (except limited pre-first-action interactions in some cases). An interview does not remove the necessity for reply to Office actions as specified in §§ 1.111 and 1.135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for using Internet electronic mail in interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet e-mail shall NOT be used to conduct an exchange or communications similar to those exchanged during telephone or personal interviews unless a written authorization has been given to use Internet e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such authorized cases, a paper copy of the Internet e-mail contents MUST be made and placed in the patent application file as required by the Federal Records Act in the same manner as an Examiner Interview Summary Form is entered. See MPEP § 502.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Conference Center (VCC) procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO has established a Video Conference Center to expedite prosecution; use requires coordination through the examiner, and appointments must be arranged at least 3 days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VCC use is currently limited to authorized off-site Patent and Trademark Depository Libraries with duplicate video equipment. The examiner will contact Patent Academy personnel to make arrangements and notify the customer of date/time. The substance of the video conference interview must be made of record in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and conduct of interviews (preparation and time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should normally be arranged in advance to ensure the primary examiner and/or examiner in charge will be present. The attorney should be fully prepared to discuss issues raised in the Office action; it is desirable to indicate in advance issues to be discussed by submitting a proposed amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should usually not be extended beyond a reasonable period, usually not longer than 30 minutes. The examiner should avoid unnecessary interruptions and may conclude the interview if no common ground can be reached or further study is required. Examiners may grant one interview after final rejection (see MPEP § 713.09). Where agreement is reached, applicant should promptly submit the agreed amendment; if amendment prepares the case for final action, examiner should take the case up as special.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prior to first official action
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing, no interview is permitted. A request for an interview prior to the first Office action is ordinarily granted in continuing or substitute applications; a request in all other applications before the first action is untimely and will not be acknowledged or granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the examiner's discretion, a limited amount of time may be spent indicating the field of search to an attorney, searcher or inventor. Searching in the group art unit should be permitted only with the consent of a primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews solely for 'sounding out' the examiner not permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews that are solely for the purpose of 'sounding out' the examiner, as by a local attorney acting for an out-of-town attorney, should not be permitted when it is apparent that any agreement reached is conditional upon being satisfactory to the principal attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner discretion should prevent interviews that are merely exploratory without proper authority or preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that substance of interview be made of record (PTOL-413)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete written statement as to the substance of any face-to-face, video conference, electronic mail or telephone interview with regard to the merits of an application must be made of record in the application, whether or not an agreement with the examiner was reached. Examiners must complete an Interview Summary form PTOL-413 for each interview where a matter of substance has been discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Interview Summary (PTOL-413) shall be given an appropriate paper number, placed in the right hand portion of the file, and listed on the 'Contents' list on the file wrapper. In a personal interview, the duplicate copy is given to the applicant at the conclusion; for telephonic/electronic/video interviews, the copy is mailed or faxed to applicant at or before the next official communication. The form provides for recordation of application number, applicant name, examiner name, date, type of interview, participants, exhibits, identification of claims and prior art discussed, whether agreement was reached, examiner signature, and other PTO personnel present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items required for complete and proper recordation of interview substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete and proper recordation of the substance of any interview should include at least the following applicable items: (A) brief description of any exhibit shown or demonstration; (B) identification of the claims discussed; (C) identification of specific prior art discussed; (D) identification of principal proposed amendments of a substantive nature discussed; (E) general thrust of principal arguments of applicant and examiner; (F) general indication of any other pertinent matters discussed; (G) if appropriate, the general results or outcome of the interview unless already described in the Interview Summary form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identification of arguments need not be lengthy or elaborate; it is sufficient if the general nature or thrust of the principal arguments can be understood in the context of the application file. Where a complete record of the interview has been incorporated in an examiner's amendment, completion of the Interview Summary form may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for making interview substance of record and correcting inaccuracies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the applicant or the attorney or agent to make the substance of an interview of record in the application file, unless the examiner indicates he or she will do so. It is the examiner’s responsibility to see that such a record is made and to correct material inaccuracies which bear directly on the question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should orally remind the applicant of his or her obligation to record the substance of the interview unless both agree the examiner will record it. Where the examiner agrees to record the substance, or when it is adequately recorded on the Interview Summary form or an attachment, the examiner will check a box informing the applicant that no supplement by the applicant is necessary.
